templates.note: Human-written sentences the nightly run fills with scraped facts. The machine substitutes dates and places; it never writes the meaning. Edit the wording here and every generated card changes with it.

note: Curated by the VP Legislation, by hand. The nightly fetch never touches this file — parent cards are written consequences, not scraped headlines. Every card needs: kid_impact (one sentence, what changes for a student/family), owner (who actually decides), and at most one action. Keep kid_impact to ONE sentence at a 4th-6th grade reading level: the single-sentence form is the one with evidence behind it, and this audience reads it in four languages. Give any dated coming_up card an 'until' (YYYY-MM-DD): the page hides it the day after, so a past meeting can never sit there saying 'coming up'. Give any card a 'covers' array of items.json ids it accounts for — the nightly gap check flags every district hot item that no card covers, so an uncovered id is a card someone still owes. If an item can't be phrased as a consequence with an owner, it stays in the VP Desk. The watchlist is VP-Desk-only: known scheduled obligations with a date they're expected by — the page flags anything past due that isn't marked done, so a blank where a report should be never goes unnoticed.

in_effect.title: Phones away during class unless staff allow them
in_effect.kid_impact: Students must silence and put away phones during class unless staff allow their use; each school sets any other permitted times.
in_effect.owner: Arcadia USD board sets the policy; each school implements it
in_effect.time_sensitivity: BP 5131.8 adopted June 23, 2026; Holly Avenue's posted elementary device rules verified October 21
in_effect.verification_note: District BP 5131.8 is adopted. Holly Avenue's website links the AUSD Elementary School Cell Phones and Smart Devices Policy (PDF posted August 2026, https://4.files.edl.io/2e5d/08/07/26/010512-daca9e8c-075c-44e4-b70e-0439c0ef9780.pdf): phones, smartwatches and other smart devices are highly discouraged, may not be used during school hours, must stay in backpacks, and parents reach students through the office or classroom staff; a device used in violation is confiscated for a parent to pick up. Consult the full policies for exceptions.
in_effect.report_summary: AUSD adopted its mobile-device policy on June 23. Holly Avenue's posted elementary rules: devices may not be used during school hours, must stay in backpacks, and parents reach students through the office. See the policies for exceptions.

in_effect.title: Board certified every student has textbooks and learning materials
in_effect.kid_impact: The board held its yearly public hearing and voted that every student has the textbooks and learning materials the state requires; tell the school office if your child is missing one.
in_effect.time_sensitivity: Public hearing and vote September 22, 2026; recording reviewed October 21
in_effect.verification_note: Agenda action item II.a: Public Hearing and Action, Resolution No. 26-27-09, Sufficiency of Instructional Materials (the Education Code 60119 annual hearing covering English, math, science and social science). Official recording transcript: hearing opened 1:13:39 with no public comments and closed 1:13:48; motion 1:14:02; vote called 1:15:15; 'Motion carries' 1:15:21. The same meeting adopted Resolution 26-27-10 (annual authorization to assign teachers to subjects not on their credential; vote 1:18:04-1:18:13) and Resolution 26-27-11 (Hispanic Heritage Month), and approved consent items A-I at 2:10:30 with none removed. Recording evidence, not signed minutes.
in_effect.report_summary: On September 22 the board held its yearly public hearing and certified that every student has sufficient textbooks and learning materials; no one spoke at the hearing. The board also renewed its annual authorization for some teachers to teach subjects outside their credential. Families who find a missing textbook should tell the school office.

in_effect.title: School improvement plans approved for every school
in_effect.kid_impact: The board approved each school's School Plan for Student Achievement, the yearly plan for how Holly Avenue will use its funds to help students learn; ask the office how to read it.
in_effect.time_sensitivity: Approved October 13, 2026 on the consent agenda; recording reviewed October 21
in_effect.verification_note: Agenda consent item IV.e, School Plans for Student Achievement (SPSA). Official recording transcript: no items removed from consent (26:54); motion to approve consent items A-E at 1:54:37; 'The motion carries' at 1:54:43; a board member's closing comment recognized the SPSA approval at 3:04:58. Also at this meeting, for information only: first reading of revised Board Policy 5141.21 on administering medication (staff proposed adding a stock albuterol inhaler program; no vote yet), and the Williams quarterly uniform-complaint summary was zero. A study session covered the district's Behavior Response Team. Recording evidence, not signed minutes; the Holly Avenue plan's contents were not reviewed here.

action.label: Ask the office how to read Holly Avenue's plan

in_effect.report_summary: On October 13 the board approved every school's School Plan for Student Achievement on the consent agenda, including Holly Avenue's. The plan's contents were not reviewed for this update; families can ask the office how to read it. The board also heard a first reading of an updated medication policy (no vote yet) and a study session on the district's Behavior Response Team.

in_effect.title: Spring 2026 state test results are out
in_effect.kid_impact: California released last spring's state test results and the 2026 School Dashboard on October 15, so families can look up how Holly Avenue did compared with the district and the state.
in_effect.time_sensitivity: Released October 15, 2026; no district statement as of October 21
in_effect.verification_note: CDE News Release #26-44 (October 15, 2026) released the 2025-26 CAASPP and ELPAC results together with the 2026 California School Dashboard; statewide, 49.3% of students met the English standard and 38.4% met the math standard. School- and district-level results are on the CAASPP results site and the Dashboard; Holly Avenue's numbers were not reviewed here, and the AUSD news feed had posted nothing since June 3.
in_effect.report_summary: California released spring 2026 state test results and the 2026 School Dashboard on October 15. Statewide, 49.3 percent of students met the English standard and 38.4 percent met the math standard. Holly Avenue's and the district's results are posted on the state sites and were not reviewed for this update; the district has not issued a statement.
